\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of space under appended choices]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_le_append}
\label{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_le_append}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w$ and $w'$ be finite
choice words, and let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input. The total number of
distinct work-tape cells visited during the run from $c$ under $w$ is at most the number
visited under the concatenated choice word $ww'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Flipping output preserves space use]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_spaceUsedWith}
\label{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_spaceUsedWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.flipCfg, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_runWith, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k$ work tapes,
let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$.
The space used by the machine with flipped output, when run under $w$ from the
configuration obtained by flipping every output bit of $c$, equals the space used by $M$
when run under $w$ from $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Space usage bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and let
$s:\\mathbb{N}\\to\\mathbb{N}$. Say that $N$ uses space bounded by $s$ if, for every
pair of Boolean lists $x,w$, the space used on work-tape input $w$ from the initial
configuration on input $x$ is at most $s(|x|)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-error space-bounded acceptance]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInSpace}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p020-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b005,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p023-b001
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p016-b001}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ decides a Boolean language $L$ in space
bounded by $s$ with bounded error if $N$ uses space at most $s$ and, for every Boolean
input $x$, there is a natural number $T$ such that $N$ halts on $x$ within $T$ steps and
its probability of outputting the indicator of membership in $L$ is at least $2/3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-error randomized space decision]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p020-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p036-b004
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p016-b001}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
A finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ decides a Boolean language $L$ in
space bounded by $s$ if it uses space at most $s$ and, for every Boolean string $x$,
there is a time bound $T$ within which it halts. If $x\in L$, its probability of
outputting true by time $T$ is at least $2/3$; if $x\notin L$, every choice sequence of
length $T$ yields the output false.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of space bounds]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, and let
$s,s'\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $N$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ space on every Boolean
input $x$ and every choice word, and $s(n)\le s'(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then
$N$ uses at most $s'(|x|)$ space on every Boolean input and every choice word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space bound from a halting time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.spaceUsedWith_le_of_haltsWithin}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.spaceUsedWith_le_of_haltsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_append_of_halt, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_le_append}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be
a binary input, and let $T,S\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every choice word of length exactly
$T$ leads to a halted configuration on $x$, and each such run uses at most $S$ work-tape
cells in total. Then every choice word, of any length, uses at most $S$ work-tape cells
in total on input $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space bound from per-input halting times]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.usesSpace_of_haltsWithin}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.usesSpace_of_haltsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.spaceUsedWith_le_of_haltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let
$s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every binary input $x$ there is a time $T$
such that every choice word of length exactly $T$ leads to a halted configuration on
$x$, and every such run uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells in total. Then for every
binary input $x$ and every choice word, the run on $x$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape
cells in total.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of bounded-error space]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInSpace.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInSpace.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.mono}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $L$ a
language of binary strings, and $s,s':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ space bounds. Suppose $N$
uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells on every input and choice word, and for each input
there is a time bound by which all branches halt and the probability of outputting the
one-bit membership value for $L$ is at least $2/3$. If $s(n)\le s'(n)$ for every $n$,
then the same machine satisfies these decision conditions with space bound $s'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the space bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.mono}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $s,s':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $s(n)\le
s'(n)$ for every $n$. If $N$ decides $L$ with the stated one-sided error guarantees
using space bound $s$, then it does so using space bound $s'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded error from one-sided error]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.bpDecidesInSpace}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.bpDecidesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_one, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every run of
$N$ on every binary input uses space at most $s$ of the input length. For each input
$x$, suppose there is a time $T$ by which every branch halts, the probability of
outputting the one-bit string $1$ is at least $2/3$ when $x\in L$, and every branch
outputs the one-bit string $0$ when $x\notin L$. Then for each input there is such a
halting time at which the probability of outputting the correct membership indicator is
at least $2/3$, while the space bound remains $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decision from one-sided error]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.decidesInSpace}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.decidesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.exists_outputWith_of_outputProb_pos, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every run on
every binary input uses space at most $s$ of its input length. For each input $x$,
suppose there is a time $T$ by which every branch halts, the probability of outputting
$1$ is at least $2/3$ if $x\in L$, and every length-$T$ branch outputs $0$ if $x\notin
L$. Then for every input $x$, there is a time $T$ by which every branch halts, every
length-$T$ branch uses space at most $s(|x|)$, and $x\in L$ exactly when some length-$T$
branch halts with output $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of randomized space]
\lean{Randomized.BPSPACE.mono}
\label{Randomized.BPSPACE.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPSPACE, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInSpace.mono}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s_1,s_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $s_1(n)\le s_2(n)$ for every $n$. Then
every language decidable with bounded error using space bounded by a constant multiple
of $s_1$ belongs to the class decidable with bounded error using space bounded by a
constant multiple of $s_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of randomized space]
\lean{Randomized.RSPACE.mono}
\label{Randomized.RSPACE.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RSPACE, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.mono}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s_1,s_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $s_1(n) \le s_2(n)$ for every $n$.
Then every language in $\mathrm{RSPACE}(s_1)$ belongs to $\mathrm{RSPACE}(s_2)$, where
membership means that a finite randomized machine uses space bounded by a constant
multiple of the given function, accepts members with probability at least $2/3$, and
never accepts nonmembers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized space is contained in bounded-error space]
\lean{Randomized.RSPACE_subset_BPSPACE}
\label{Randomized.RSPACE_subset_BPSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPSPACE, Randomized.RSPACE, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.bpDecidesInSpace}
\difficulty{3}
For every function $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{RSPACE}(s) \subseteq
\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s)$. Here $\mathrm{RSPACE}(s)$ uses finite randomized machines with
space bounded by a constant multiple of $s$, acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on
members, and no accepting branches on nonmembers; $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s)$ uses such a
space bound and outputs the correct membership bit with probability at least $2/3$ on
every input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized Logspace Is Contained in Bounded-Error Logspace]
\lean{Randomized.RL_subset_BPL}
\label{Randomized.RL_subset_BPL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace, Randomized.BPL, Randomized.RL, Randomized.RSPACE_subset_BPSPACE}
\difficulty{1}
Every language of Boolean strings decidable in randomized logspace with one-sided error
is decidable in bounded-error randomized logspace: there is a constant-factor logspace
machine that halts within a finite time bound on every input and outputs the correct
membership bit with probability at least $2/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized space is contained in nondeterministic space]
\lean{Randomized.RSPACE_subset_NSPACE}
\label{Randomized.RSPACE_subset_NSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NSPACE, Randomized.RSPACE, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInSpace.decidesInSpace}
\difficulty{3}
For every function $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{RSPACE}(s) \subseteq
\mathrm{NSPACE}(s)$. The randomized class requires a finite machine using space bounded
by a constant multiple of $s$, with acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members and
no accepting branches on nonmembers; the nondeterministic class requires a finite
machine with that space bound that halts on every branch and accepts exactly the
members.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized Logspace Is Contained in Nondeterministic Logspace]
\lean{Randomized.RL_subset_NL}

\difficulty{1}
Every language decidable by a randomized Turing machine using logarithmic space, halting
on every input within some finite input-dependent number of steps, with acceptance
probability at least $2/3$ on members and no accepting branch on nonmembers, is
decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine using logarithmic space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized Logspace Is Contained in Polynomial Time]
\lean{Randomized.RL_subset_P}

\difficulty{1}
Every language decidable by a randomized Turing machine using logarithmic space, halting
on every input within some finite input-dependent number of steps, with acceptance
probability at least $2/3$ on members and no accepting branch on nonmembers, is
decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability one implies universal satisfaction]
\lean{Randomized.forall_of_randProb_eq_one}

\difficulty{5}

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work tape count bounded by space]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.k_le}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.k_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let
$s\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean input $x$ and every
choice word $w$, the total number of work tape cells visited along the run from the
initial configuration on $x$ is at most $s(|x|)$. Then $k\le s(n)$ for every

\begin{theorem}[Space bound for the amplified machine]

\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, and suppose that on every input and
every choice string its total space use is at most $s(n)$, where $n$ is the input
length. For every natural number $r$ and every decision function on the run count, the
amplified machine formed using $r$ has total space use at most $3(r+1)k_Ns(n)$ on inputs

\begin{theorem}[Amplification of a Randomized Decision Procedure]
\lean{Randomized.exists_rDecides_of_pos}
\label{Randomized.exists_rDecides_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.acc, Randomized.Amplify.amp, Randomized.Amplify.amp_haltsWithin, Randomized.Amplify.amp_outputProb, Randomized.amp_usesSpace_mul, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.exists_ofFn_eq, Randomized.forall_of_randProb_eq_one, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_blockCount, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_false, Randomized.randProb_le_one, Randomized.randProb_not, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$
be a language of Boolean lists, let $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let
$\delta,\varepsilon$ be positive rational numbers. Suppose $N$ uses space at most
$s(|x|)$ on every input $x$ and every choice word. Suppose also that for each input $x$
there is a time bound $T$ such that every choice word of length $T$ halts; if $x \in L$,
the probability of output $[\mathrm{true}]$ at time $T$ is at least $\delta$; and if $x
\notin L$, every choice word of length $T$ produces output $[\mathrm{false}]$. Then
there are a natural number $a$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N'$ over
the Boolean alphabet that uses space at most $a s(|x|)$ on every input and choice word,
and such that for each input $x$ there is a time bound $T$ at which every choice word
halts, the probability of output $[\mathrm{true}]$ is at least $1-\varepsilon$ when $x
\in L$, and every choice word produces output $[\mathrm{false}]$ when $x \notin L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Amplifying a randomized decision advantage]
\lean{Randomized.exists_bpDecides_of_advantage}
\label{Randomized.exists_bpDecides_of_advantage}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Amplify.amp, Randomized.Amplify.amp_haltsWithin, Randomized.Amplify.amp_outputProb, Randomized.Amplify.majority_randProb_ge, Randomized.amp_usesSpace_mul, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $L$ be a language of bit
strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $\delta,\varepsilon$ are positive
rational numbers, $N$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ space on every input and choice word, and
for each input $x$ there is a time bound $T$ such that every choice word of length $T$
makes $N$ halt and the probability that it outputs the indicator of membership of $x$ in
$L$ is at least $\frac12+\delta$. Then there are a natural number $a$ and a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine $N'$ using at most $a s(|x|)$ space such that, for every
$x$, some time bound $T$ makes every choice word of length $T$ halt and the probability
that $N'$ outputs the membership indicator of $x$ in $L$ is at least $1-\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive Acceptance Probability Implies RSPACE]
\lean{Randomized.mem_RSPACE_of_pos}
\label{Randomized.mem_RSPACE_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RSPACE, Randomized.exists_rDecides_of_pos, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.mono, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $L$ be a language of bit
strings, let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and let $c\in\mathbb{N}$ and
$\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ with $0<\delta$. Suppose that on every input $x$, some time bound
$T$ ensures halting on every branch; on members, the probability of outputting $[1]$
within that bound is at least $\delta$; and on nonmembers, every choice string of length
$T$ yields output $[0]$. Suppose also that the space used on every input and choice
string is at most $c s(|x|)$. Then $L$ belongs to $\mathrm{RSPACE}(s)$, the class with a
constant-multiple space bound, halting on every branch within an input-dependent finite
time, acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members, and certain rejection on
nonmembers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive Advantage Implies Bounded-Space Recognition]
\lean{Randomized.mem_BPSPACE_of_advantage}
\label{Randomized.mem_BPSPACE_of_advantage}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPSPACE, Randomized.exists_bpDecides_of_advantage, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace.mono, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $L$ be a language of bit
strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, $c\in\mathbb{N}$, and
$\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\delta$. Suppose that on every input $x$, every choice
string of some length $T$ leads $N$ to halt, and the probability that its output equals
the Boolean indicator of membership of $x$ in $L$ is at least $1/2+\delta$. Suppose also
that on every input and every choice string, the total number of distinct work-tape
cells visited is at most $c s(|x|)$. Then $L$ belongs to $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s)$, meaning
that some finite nondeterministic Turing machine uses at most a constant multiple of
$s(|x|)$ space, halts on every branch within an input-dependent finite time, and outputs
the correct membership indicator with probability at least $2/3$.
\end{theorem}
